projects.title: Ideas I turned into projects
projects.subtitle: Here are four ways I’ve put what I learned into practice: an app for a clinic, a first game, the portfolio you’re browsing, and a dashboard for analyzing bike rentals.
projects.empty: There are no projects available in this category.

clinic.description: A desktop application for managing patient records and medical visits and tracking BMI over time.

story.objective: The team built this project for the Applied Programming Tools III course at the Technological University of Panama to apply what they learned to clinical record management.
story.solution: The application manages patient records and logs medical visits. It calculates and classifies BMI from weight and height, charts each patient’s BMI over time, and summarizes statistics in an overall report.
story.technologies: The application logic is written in C# and runs on .NET 10. Windows Forms provides the desktop interface, and Azure SQL Database stores patient records, medical visits, and BMI classification ranges.

firstGame.description: A C++ console maze game where you guide a character to the treasure.

story.objective: Reach the treasure ($) by navigating a maze drawn with characters in the console.
story.solution: The game loads the maze from Map.txt and reads the intro and victory screens from text files. Each WASD command attempts to move the character one cell. Reaching the treasure brings up the victory screen.
story.technologies: The game uses C++ and its standard library for file reading and console input and output. The Code::Blocks project is configured for GNU GCC.
story.learning: The code shows how to divide responsibilities among the Player, GameMap, and MapCell classes, load text resources, and validate each move to keep the character from walking through walls or leaving the map.

bikeSharing.imageAlt: Bike Sharing Analytics overview showing 3.29 million rentals and charts of monthly and hourly rentals.
bikeSharing.description: An interactive dashboard covering 3.29 million historical Capital Bikeshare rentals, with demand and weather analysis and machine learning model evaluation.

portfolio.imageAlt: Giovanny Arpaia’s portfolio homepage, with his name and main links.
portfolio.description: A personal portfolio originally built with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, now being modernized with React and Tailwind CSS.

story.objective: Modernize the original portfolio and present the projects in Spanish, English, and Italian.
story.solution: The page is organized into sections, and the project catalog uses reusable cards with category filters.
story.technologies: React composes the sections, Tailwind CSS styles them, and i18next manages translations.
story.learning: Keep the catalog available if GitHub fails. The cards use local data, then show the language and star count when the API responds.
